sentences.text: Rauisuchus, meaning "Wilhelm Rau's crocodile," is an extinct genus of archosaurs that lived in Brazil between 235 and 228 million years ago.
This animal is distinguished by a knob-like thickening on the premaxilla, short ventrally keeled cervical vertebrae, and elongated caudals with specific neural spines and laminae.
Dr. Wilhelm Rau discovered Rauisuchus remains near the road from Santa Maria to San Jose in 1928 or 1929 while working under Friedrich von Huene.
The discovery site, known as Zahnsanga, was located 20 to 30 meters from the road and was likely a ravine or escarpment.
Krebs described the tarsus of R. tiradentes in 1973, and the lectotype was assigned in 1976.
Lautenschlager and Rauhut removed remains from Locality 15, known as Find 1020, from the genus in 2014 because they could not be diagnostically assigned to Rauisuchus.
Rauisuchids were top predators that ate other reptiles and possibly hunted early dinosaurs.
Rauisuchus belongs to the Rauisuchidae, a group of land-dwelling crocodile relatives, though it was initially assigned to the Theriodontia in 1936.
Rauisuchus is placed as the sister taxon to Tikisuchus and Yarasuchus, forming a clade with them.
